ledger.claim: This dispute is filed by the RIDER and the fare ledger shows payment_status 'CHARGED' with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the $2.00 ERP line is still being carried by the rider and has not been returned. A refund of that line is therefore a real remedy on this record, whereas NO_ACTION would leave the disputed charge standing against the filing party.

The one and only ERP line on this trip is 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at $2.00, and the driver's own 108-fix, 100%-coverage trace never comes near it: the nearest fix is 6,130.08 m from the gantry, far outside the 250 m radius by which POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace. On that match test the vehicle never crossed this gantry at all, so the line is a billing-integrity failure refundable in full under POL-RD-09(4).

The fare ledger itself flags the gantry 'on_optimal_route': false, and the trip record's own optimal route carries optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00 — the platform's own routing says the optimal route crosses no ERP gantry at all. The off-optimal-route ERP total is $2.00 against an on-optimal-route total of $0.00. A $2.00 charge on a corridor the optimal route never uses, and which the trace never visits, is exactly the off-corridor pass-through POL-RD-09 exists to correct.

The rider does not need to prove a route deviation to recover the ERP line. POL-RD-01 provides that a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) is available whether or not a deviation exists, and on the governing trace figure the excess is only 0.65 km / 5.00% against the 0.8 km and 20% gates — so the ERP correction stands on its own footing either way.

The driver's only answer on the record is that 'the ERP is charged by the system' — a bare assertion naming no evidence ID and no artifact showing the vehicle ever crossed the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded; it cannot overcome a trace whose nearest approach to the charged gantry is 6,130.08 m.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-02815-01, is admissibility MISSING, carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0, and has no payload, so it can be cited only for its absence. POL-RD-03 exoneration requires an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses; with none on file there is no record-based justification for any off-corridor ERP charge.

The correct disposition is a ruled refund, not a held file. The unmatched gantry line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09 provides that POL-RD-10(8) is not thereby triggered. Even if the driver's 'charged by the system' were read as an external-cause assertion, it names no advisory identifier, and under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged: the missing advisory (EV-ADVIS-02815-01, admissibility MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction within it. The rider should receive the $2.00 as a stand-alone billing-integrity correction, with the billing-integrity referral recorded alongside the money.

The route-deviation claim fails at the threshold and fails on the governing field. The trace, not the rounded trip record, measures this trip: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 13.65 km against a booked optimal of 13.0 km, an excess of 0.65 km and 5.0%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests must pass and neither does — 0.65 km is under the 0.8 km absolute gate and 5.0% is under the 20% proportional gate. The derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. No deviation is established on this trip, however the rider characterises the road taken.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 is never reached: there is no recomputation of the optimal-route fare and therefore no distance-or-time refund of any size. The metered distance charge of 10.28 and time charge of 4.98 computed on this trip's actuals stand, and the rider's contested figure of $4.00 cannot be recovered on a route-deviation theory.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trace is unimpaired on the POL-RD-07 tests — 108 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire, no independent corroboration is needed, and the trace stands as the measurement. On that unimpaired trace no excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold, so the driver has nothing to answer.

POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation check does not fire, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral can follow from it. The driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are 0 over 388 completed trips: the count limb (3 or more) and the ratio limb (0.05 or more on at least 40 trips) both fail on the fields the clause names. POL-RD-06 is in any event consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation, and this trip's 0.65 km excess — 5.0% — is nowhere near the 50% or 8.0 km materiality gate.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest, POL-RD-09 confines any correction to the government-set pass-through lines itemised on the fare ledger and settles them separately from distance and time; POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting such a line inside any distance refund, and since POL-RD-02 does not run the rider can reach no distance or time money at all. The most any pass-through correction could touch is the single $2.00 AYE Alexandra Rd gantry line; the remaining $2.00 of the $4.00 contested corresponds to no identified line of the fare breakdown.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. Your dispute was over $4.00, and $2.00 of it is returned to the rider.

Route deviation — not established. The measurement that governs is the GPS trace, 13.65 km, not the trip record's rounded 13.7 km. Against the booked optimal of 13.0 km the excess is 0.65 km, or 5.0%, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal. Neither gate is passed, so no deviation exists, POL-RD-02 is never reached, and no distance or time refund is due. The driver's submissions on this point are accepted in full.

The ERP line — $2.00 refunded. The fare ledger carries a single ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry', at $2.00. That gantry carries coordinates, and the driver's own trace (108 fixes, 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps) never comes within the 250 m match radius of it — the nearest fix is 6,130.08 m away, on a Yishun-to-Bishan trip that runs nowhere near the AYE. The vehicle never crossed this gantry. POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction and available whether or not a deviation exists. The rider's claim succeeds on this line and $2.00 is returned. The driver's statement that 'the ERP is charged by the system' names no evidence ID and no clause; under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not show a crossing.

The rest of the $4.00 — the remaining $2.00 of the contested amount corresponds to no identified line of the fare breakdown, so it is not refunded.

Figures used: charged_total $21.86; the refunded ERP line $2.00; optimal_route_erp_sgd $0.00; traced excess 0.65 km / 5.0%; amount contested $4.00.

No escalation. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); the trip identifiers all match; the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the one already refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09 states does not trigger POL-RD-10(8); and no party has invoked the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-02815-01 (admissibility MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) as an excuse — it is cited only for its absence, so POL-RD-13(1) and POL-RD-10(5) do not engage.

The ruling rests on the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, both at weight 1.0, so it is not discounted on confidence. The POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral rides alongside the money and does not displace it. This ruling is provisional; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' ERP line of $2.00 on TRP-02815 is charged for a gantry the GPS trace never crosses (nearest fix 6,130.08 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius); record it as a billing-integrity finding, refund it as a standalone pass-through correction, and review why the line was charged.
